headlines.headline: USTR's 60-Economy Section 301 Tariffs (10–12.5%) Take Effect — Replaces Struck-Down IEEPA Regime
headlines.driver: For XLI (Industrials, Main proxy): Positive — rebuilds tariff wall on sturdier 301 footing after 6-3 loss; XLI's constituents (defense, machinery) gain pricing power and import protection, and TRQs reward US-cotton sourcing — directly lifts XLI's order books vs XLB.

headlines.headline: China Semiconductor Stack Nears 70%: 50% IP + 12.5% Forced Labor + 7.5% Overcapacity Before Sept 24 Summit
headlines.driver: For XLI: Positive — 70% stack on China semis protects US industrials' chip supply chain and justifies reshoring capex that flows to XLI names (automation, robotics in 22 sectors). Negative for XLI's China-exposed supply, but net pricing power for domestic XLI.

headlines.headline: Section 338: US Slaps 50% on ~5% of Canada Imports; Canada Dollar-for-Dollar Retaliation Sep 8 — USMCA at Risk
headlines.driver: For XLI: Mixed — 50% on ~5% of Canada imports is surgically narrow but hits XLI's auto/aero supply chains Jan 1 2027; Canada retaliation risks USMCA withdrawal volatility for XLI's cross-border manufacturers, but near-term industrials pricing up as imports fall.

headlines.headline: $100B Tariff Refunds Flatter Q3 Earnings — Walmart $2.9B, Apple $2.2B, But No Consumer Pass-Through Yet
headlines.driver: For XLI: Positive near-term — $100B refund is direct cash to XLI importers (Ford $1.3B) boosting Q3 EPS and cash flow for buybacks; but refunds are one-time, so XLI's underlying demand (ISM 50.3) matters more than headline EPS.

headlines.headline: 82% of Manufacturers Now Passing Tariff Costs — Absorption Buffer Exhausted, Margin Compression Next
headlines.driver: For XLI: Positive for pricing, negative for volume — 82% pass-through (vs 44%) means XLI's constituents finally have pricing power, but 4.2% of primary metal inputs and Yale 9.6% effective rate mean margin compression ahead for XLI's SME suppliers, raising distress risk in XLI's supply chain.

headlines.headline: Tariff Decoupling Hits Ceiling at ~33% Effective — $30B Non-Strategic Relief Valve vs Strategic Hold
headlines.driver: For XLI: Neutral — 33% effective ceiling shows supply-chain interdependence limits decoupling; XLI's $30B non-strategic relief is narrow, so XLI's large caps with on-shore capacity win, while China-plus-one assemblers in XLI see limited benefit.

headlines.headline: Tariffs Wedge Industrials vs Materials: XLB Breaks Out, XLI $179→$185 on Defense/Capex vs Steel Pricing Power
headlines.driver: For XLI: Positive — XLI $179→$185 forecast on defense capex ($850B) vs XLB commodity pricing shows XLI's driver is capex resilience, not just steel price; XLI-XLB spread tells which tariff channel dominates XLI's return.
